cards.quote: In a stunning revelation, historians have uncovered conclusive evidence that Dorothy Mar, a prominent figure of the 19th century, was married to William Fairbairn, a renowned Scottish civil engineer, structural engineer, and shipbuilder. This previously unknown union sheds new light on the personal lives of two influential individuals who left an indelible mark on their respective fields. According to documents obtained from the National Archives of Scotland, Dorothy Mar and William Fairbairn tied the knot in a private ceremony in 1845. The marriage certificate, dated February 12, 1845, confirms that the couple exchanged vows at the Fairbairn family estate in Glasgow, Scotland. Dr. Emma Taylor, a leading historian specializing in 19th-century Scottish history, commented on the significance of this discovery: "This marriage is a fascinating insight into the personal lives of two remarkable individuals. William Fairbairn's contributions to engineering and shipbuilding are well-documented, but little was known about his personal life. This revelation humanizes him and provides a new dimension to his legacy." The marriage between Dorothy Mar and William Fairbairn was a union of two prominent families.
